state:
Goal `core-str-3-3`: `startsWith`, `trim`, `trimStart` and `trimEnd` now have every feature
proof on disk: description, three examples each, an attack, a bench record, a Rust test with
their `covers:` markers, and cards in plain words. The attack on `trim` found a quadratic cost:
`trimmed` searched the whole `characters` set once for each character it removed, so a 1 MiB set
against a 1 MiB subject took minutes. `trimmed` now reads the set once into a `TrimSet` (an
ASCII bitmask, and a sorted list of the other characters, paid for through
`nvs_runtime::affordable`). `tests/conformance/core/str-trim-matches-a-long-or-multi-byte-set-by-character.nvst`
pins it. Every `Core\Str` perf record was re-measured after `str.rs` changed. The members still
owed in this goal are `upper`, `upperFirst` and `wrap`.

next.title: member proofs, file order
next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs`, and each member's trees under `docs/examples/core/Str/`, `tests/hostile/core/Str/`, `benches/members/core/Str/`.

items.text: **`Core\Str::upper`, `upperFirst`** — each owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). `lower` and `lowerFirst` are the twins to copy the shape from. Check that a character whose upper case is longer (`ß` becomes `SS`) is paid for before the result is built. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3514`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3526`

**`Core\Str::wrap`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Its result can be much longer than its input (a width of 1 adds a break after every character), so check that the output is paid for before it is built, and attack it with a width of 1 on a long text. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3276`

next.after: Once all three are green, the goal's check `dossier-core-str-3-3` should pass: run `bun nv verify --doc`, `bun nv owners --closes core-str-3-3` and `bun nv playbook --closes core-str-3-3` and write `DONE`.

backlog: `trim`'s set matches by code point, not by grapheme: trimming `e` from `"ee\u{301}t"` leaves a lone combining accent at the start (`tests/hostile/core/Str/trimStart/01-a-long-run-before-one-character.nvs` step 2). It is PHP's behaviour and the card says "character"; whether a grapheme-matched set is wanted belongs to `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs`'s `trimmed` doc, and no gap is recorded.
